free_tier.stated: 8 GB free for one user, with no payment method required. Paid: 128 GB at EUR 7.44/month, up to 1 TB on the personal ladder; business plans from EUR 61/month with 1 TB to 100 TB

per_object_cap.stated: Not published for the free 8 GB plan

retention.stated: Until deleted. No retention clock published

egress.terms: 'Share transfer unlimited' on the free tier; traffic is not metered on the paid plans

tooling: rclone webdav and the Nextcloud clients. Nextcloud Hub with Talk and Collabora on the paid plans
chaining: 8 GB needs no payment method at all, which makes it the cheapest way to obtain an EU Nextcloud shard with zero identity cost beyond an email address. It cannot reach 500 GB without 60-plus accounts, and the provider manages users centrally on paid plans, so the shard path is per-account only

limits.value: the free plan is one user and 8 GB, and Talk with end-to-end encryption are paid-plan features

identity_cost.detail: an email address and no payment method, per 'Take a free account. No payment method required, just try it'

reliability_note: Milan and the Netherlands. The free 8 GB plan was explicitly confirmed as surviving a July 2026 repricing, which is rare and worth recording: 'Q: Is the free 8 GB account going away? A: No.'

evidence.proved: 'Nextcloud One, 1 person, EUR 7,44 per month'; 'Business per 50 users from EUR 61 per month'; storage 'up to 100TB'; 'Take a free account. No payment method required, just try it'
'Q: Is the free 8 GB account going away? A: No. The free 8 GB plan remains available.' beside a 2026-07-01 price-change notice

binding_note: The gate worth naming is that the free tier is a single user with no quota controls, so it cannot even be sharded internally.
confidence_note: The specific claim that would be worth re-checking live is that the free tier survived the July 2026 repricing.
notes: Recorded because the free tier survived a repricing, which is the opposite of the pattern everywhere else in this topic, and because it needs no card. It is a test endpoint and not capacity.
